Claude Code removes that entry after the last worktree is removed, but only if Claude Code added it. It never removes a value you set yourself. Before v2.1.207, the entry remained after the last worktree was removed, and go-git-based tools such as `tea` failed to open the repository until you ran `git config --unset extensions.worktreeConfig`." The second/third/fourth sentences reinforce rather than reverse the claim, and settings.md:372 carries the enabling half and links back to this section. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY, not assumed: on git 2.43.0 I built a scratch repo, added a linked worktree with `--no-checkout`, ran exactly our argv `git -C <wt> sparse-checkout set --cone pkg/a` -- the shared `.git/config` gained `[extensions] worktreeConfig = true` (absent before both `worktree add` and the sparse-set) -- then ran `git worktree remove <wt>`, removing the LAST worktree: the entry is still `true`. Nothing upstream handles it either: the only other removal path, `WorktreeLeaseService.sweepOrphans`/`release` (worktree-lease-service.ts:146-192, :331), routes through the same `git.remove` closure. correctedState: Confirmed as claimed, with three refinements. (a) The divergence is gated on an opt-in setting: `worktree.sparsePaths` defaults to `[]` (WORKTREE_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS, worktree-settings.ts:71-76), and worktreeCreateCommands returns early with no sparse-set when the list is empty (worktree-git-plan.ts:84), so an unconfigured user never triggers it. It reproduces for any user who sets `worktree.sparsePaths` in config.json (read live per operation via getUserWorktreeSettings, SessionManager.ts:10116; parsed at storage.ts:1313). (b) The consequence is measured, not inferred: on git 2.43.0 our exact argv writes `[extensions] worktreeConfig = true` into the shared `.git/config`, and removing the last worktree leaves it -- git does not clean it up, so the doc's go-git failure state persists in the user's main checkout after Nessy is done. (c) Closing it needs three parts our code has none of, matching the doc's 'only if Claude Code added it' carve-out: read `extensions.worktreeConfig` before the first sparse-set and record whether we enabled it, count remaining worktrees at remove time, and `git config --unset extensions.worktreeConfig` only when we own it and the count reaches zero -- with the added wrinkle that Nessy leases are per-session under one shared namespace root, so 'last worktree' must be computed across sessions (via `git worktree list`), not per WorktreeLeaseService instance.
